Subject: Acme Security Questionnaire: hosted API data residency & retention

Hi Rohaan,

We're working through the security questionnaire for our upcoming procurement review and need some concise answers around data residency, retention, and deletion for Redwood's hosted API. The questionnaire has a few specific asks but to start can you confirm at a high level:

1) Where customer request payloads and generated outputs are stored (region and tiering).
2) Default retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and any cached KV or prefix caches.
3) Deletion/erasure process and the SLA we can commit to for logical deletion and full removal from backups.
4) Do you support per-tenant geo-lock (preventing cross-region backups for an account) on hosted API, or is that only for Dedicated/Private?
5) Backup snapshot retention and whether snapshots are encrypted with separate tenant keys.

Acme would appreciate an answer in bullet form plus any evidence (diagram, retention matrix) you can attach. Our procurement team is on a tight schedule.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Huang

Claire — thanks for the clear list. Below is an initial summary; we'll attach the retention matrix and a simplified dataflow diagram in my next message. Marissa and Priyom are copied for accuracy and can add infra/ops specifics.

Summary (hosted API):
- Storage location: customer request payloads and generated outputs are persisted in the primary region assigned to your account (default for Acme: us-west-2). We route and store live data in-region; auxiliary tooling (metrics indexing, analytics) may replicate metadata to a secondary region for operational telemetry only.
- Default retention windows:
  • Request/interaction logs (text payloads + metadata): 14 days by default. Can be extended via contract up to 90 days.
  • Embeddings and vector indexes: 60 days default; customers may opt-in to longer retention for search use-cases.
  • KV/prefix caches and ephemeral session state: kept in-memory and persisted for up to 7 days by default to support streaming resumes; not used for long-term storage.
  • System/operational logs (audit, infra): retained for 180 days for incident investigation and compliance.
- Erasure / deletion process and timelines:
  • Logical deletion (live dataset & indexes): 0–24 hours from request — immediate logical unlinking from tenant view and KV cache invalidation.
  • Background physical purge (live store + reindexed shards): typically within 7 business days.
  • Snapshot / backup removal: snapshots are on a 30-day rolling retention by default; full removal from snapshot stores can take up to 30 days after the purge window.
- Geo-lock capability: hosted API supports regional tenancy routing (we pin live storage and ingress to a region), but for strict per-tenant geo-lock (blocking cross-region backups and replication guarantees at the storage-layer) we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private. Hosted customers can request stronger controls on a case-by-case basis (and we document any exceptions in the contract).
- Encryption: all persisted data is encrypted at rest; snapshots are encrypted with service-managed keys. Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) / tenant-scoped KMS is available for Dedicated and Private.

I'll send the retention matrix and a short diagram next. If you want a guaranteed deletion SLA beyond the timelines above we can escalate to a contract amendment for Acme's procurement.

— Rohaan Mehta
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Claire — attaching the two artifacts you requested and adding more precise definitions and evidence types below. Marissa / Priyom added infra-level notes inline.

Attachments (included):
- hostedapi-retention-matrix.pdf (matrix by data class and default + contractual options)
- redwood-hosted-dataflow-diagram.png (simplified flow: ingress -> transient cache -> primary region store -> snapshot lifecycle)

Definitions and evidence we can provide:
- Logical deletion: an API-level operation that immediately dereferences and marks tenant objects as deleted in the live index. This action is synchronous and returns a deletion event id. Evidence: deletion event id, request timestamp, API audit log entry.
- Physical purge: background work that reclaims underlying storage blocks and removes entries from indexes and local replicas. This is what prevents recovery from live stores. Evidence: purge job run id, shard-level purge confirmation entries in our audit index. Typical timing: 7 business days from request (can be faster with an accelerated purge request; see below).
- Snapshots/backups: default behavior for hosted API is rolling snapshots retained in the primary region for 30 days. For disaster recovery we keep a single encrypted replica in a DR region for a subset of metadata (not full raw payloads) — this is limited and under strict access controls; replication is for operational continuity and is not used for analytics or third-party processing. Evidence: snapshot manifest entries, storage bucket object logs, and KMS key usage logs.
- Accelerated purge request: Acme may request an expedited purge for a specific tenant dataset. For hosted API we can prioritize the purge pipeline and attempt to complete physical purge within 72 hours of request; practical limits: if data is contained in immutable long-term archival snapshots (rare for hosted API) we may need up to 30 days and will provide an exception log. An expedited purge commitment should be added to your contract for guaranteed SLA.
- Audit trails and attestation: we provide API-level audit logs (activity, deletion event ids), snapshot manifests, and a deletion confirmation package (job ids + timestamps + storage manifests). For customers requiring formal attestation we offer an add-on that includes a signed erasure report.

Infra notes (Marissa / Priyom):
- marissa_cole: "Snapshots are encrypted with service-managed keys for hosted customers; we do not currently support tenant-specific KMS on hosted API. Snapshot replication to DR includes metadata manifests only; full payload replication is only for Dedicated/Private."
- priyom_das: "Deletion event flows trigger cache invalidation across the serving tier immediately. Purge jobs are idempotent and audited; we retain purge logs for 180 days."

Next steps: we can schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra and security SMEs (Marissa, Priyom) to walk Acme's security team through the artifacts and provide a bespoke purge SLA if your legal team requires it.

Best,
Rohaan Mehta
